## What does PrismCrawl Yelp API do?

**PrismCrawl Yelp API** looks up **Yelp businesses** by keyword and location, and collects **complete Yelp reviews** for any business, through the PrismCrawl API. Business results include **name, rating, review count, price, categories, neighborhood, coordinates, and photos**; reviews include **rating, text, author, date, and photos**.

This Actor is a thin integration between Apify and PrismCrawl. It does not scrape anything itself: every request is executed by the [PrismCrawl API](https://www.prismcrawl.com/docs), and the Actor passes your parameters through and stores what PrismCrawl returns. PrismCrawl requests are **live and uncached**.

Running it on Apify adds scheduling, API access, webhooks and integrations, run monitoring, and dataset exports on top of PrismCrawl.

- 🌐 PrismCrawl website: [www.prismcrawl.com](https://www.prismcrawl.com/)
- 📖 Full API reference: [www.prismcrawl.com/docs](https://www.prismcrawl.com/docs)

## Why use PrismCrawl Yelp API?

- **Local lead generation**: list businesses of a type in any city.
- **Reputation monitoring**: collect new reviews for your locations or competitors on a schedule.
- **Market research**: compare ratings and price levels across an area.
- **No infrastructure**: PrismCrawl handles retrieval and parsing, so you don't run browsers, proxies, or parsers.

## You need a PrismCrawl API key

This Actor uses **your own PrismCrawl account**. To get a key:

1. Create a free account at [prismcrawl.com](https://www.prismcrawl.com/auth). New accounts get **100 free credits** and don't need a credit card.
2. Copy your API key from the PrismCrawl dashboard.
3. Paste it into the **PrismCrawl API key** field of this Actor.

The key field is a **secret input**: Apify stores it encrypted, and the Actor never logs it or writes it to the dataset. It is only sent to `api.prismcrawl.com` in the `x-api-key` header.

## How much does it cost to get Yelp businesses and reviews with PrismCrawl?

There are two separate costs:

- **PrismCrawl credits** (billed by PrismCrawl to your PrismCrawl account). **Each successful request costs one credit**, including a completed request that returns no results. Each additional page is a separate request. **Failed requests are free**: invalid requests, authentication errors, rate limits, and server errors don't use credits. PrismCrawl sells prepaid credit packages with no subscription. See [PrismCrawl pricing](https://www.prismcrawl.com/serp-api/pricing) for current packages and rates.
- **Apify platform usage** (billed by Apify) for the Actor's compute time. The Actor only makes HTTP calls, so a run is short and uses very little memory.

With **Maximum pages** set to 1 (the default), one run uses at most one PrismCrawl credit.

## How to use PrismCrawl Yelp API

1. Open the Actor's **Input** tab.
2. Paste your **PrismCrawl API key**.
3. Choose **What to fetch** and fill in the fields for that mode.
4. Optionally adjust the other settings.
5. Click **Start**. When the run finishes, open the **Output** tab to see the results.

You can also start the Actor through the [Apify API](https://docs.apify.com/api/v2), schedule it, or connect it to webhooks and integrations.

## Input

Parameter names in the table are the PrismCrawl API names, so you can look each one up in the [PrismCrawl API reference](https://www.prismcrawl.com/docs).

| Field | PrismCrawl parameter | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PrismCrawl API key | `x-api-key` header | Your secret PrismCrawl key. Required. |
| What to fetch | – | `search` (business lookup) or `reviews`. |
| Search query | `query` | For business lookup. |
| Location or Latitude / Longitude | `location` / `coordinates` | For business lookup: exactly one is required. |
| Business alias | `id` | For reviews, such as `halcyon-austin-2`. |
| Review order | `sort_by` | For reviews: `recommended`, `newest`, `oldest`, `highest_rating`, `lowest_rating`. |
| Maximum pages | – | Pages to fetch (1–100, default 1). Each page uses one credit. |
| First page | `page` | One-based page to start from. |
| Items per page | `limit` | 1–100. |
| Language / Device | `language` / `device` | For example `en`, `mobile`. |
| Zero trace | `zero_trace` | PrismCrawl won't store the source or parsed response; only audit and billing metadata is kept. |

Business lookup covers Yelp's first 200 businesses for a search, so `(page - 1) × limit` must be under 200. Fields that don't apply to the selected mode are ignored, and the run log lists them.

The Actor checks the input before sending anything, so invalid input fails immediately and costs nothing.

### Example input

```json
{
    "prismcrawlApiKey": "<YOUR_PRISMCRAWL_API_KEY>",
    "mode": "search",
    "location": "Austin, TX",
    "query": "restaurants",
    "limit": 20,
    "maxPages": 3
}
```

## Output

The Actor stores **one dataset item per page**. Each item is the **PrismCrawl response exactly as returned**, plus two fields added by the Actor:

- `page`: the page number within this run (1, 2, …)
- `credits_remaining`: your remaining PrismCrawl credits, from the `X-Credits-Remaining` response header

The **Output** tab has these views of the same data:

- **Businesses**: one row per business (business lookup).
- **Reviews**: one row per review.
- **Pages**: one row per PrismCrawl request with the complete response

You can download the dataset in various formats such as JSON, HTML, CSV, or Excel.

### Example output item

Illustrative example with the documented response structure, shortened; live values vary.

```json
{
    "page": 1,
    "credits_remaining": 99,
    "success": true,
    "request_id": "66ca8deb-1dc2-4017-865f-c4fb0e3c7c0d",
    "data": {
        "format": "json",
        "content": {
            "search_parameters": {
                "engine": "yelp",
                "type": "search"
            },
            "results": [
                {
                    "id": "<business alias>",
                    "rank": 1,
                    "title": "Example Cafe",
                    "rating": 4.5,
                    "review_count": 210,
                    "price": "$$",
                    "city": "Austin",
                    "url": "https://www.yelp.com/biz/<business alias>"
                }
            ],
            "has_next_page": false,
            "serp_features": []
        }
    }
}
```

### Main data fields

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `request_id` | PrismCrawl request ID. Use it to find the request in your PrismCrawl request history or when contacting support. |
| `data.content.results[]` (lookup) | Businesses: `id`, `business_id`, `title`, `rating`, `review_count`, `price`, `categories`, `city`, `neighborhoods`, `coordinates`, `snippet`, `photos`, `url`. |
| `data.content.results[]` (reviews) | Reviews: `rating`, `text`, `author`, `date`, `photos`. |
| `data.content.search_parameters` | Includes `location_not_found`, `source_result_count`, and `review_count` when relevant. |

The full, authoritative schema is in the [PrismCrawl API reference](https://www.prismcrawl.com/docs).

## Tips and advanced options

- **Control cost with Maximum pages.** Each page is one credit. Start with 1 page and increase only if you need more. Later pages increase `page` by 1.
- **Get business aliases from a lookup**: each result's Yelp URL ends with its alias.
- **Use Zero trace for sensitive requests.** PrismCrawl then keeps only audit and billing metadata. Results still appear in your Apify dataset.
- **Standby (HTTP) mode.** For low-latency calls from your own code, use the Actor's Standby URL: `POST /` with the same JSON fields as the input (without `prismcrawlApiKey` and `maxPages`), and send your PrismCrawl key in the `x-prismcrawl-api-key` header. The response is the PrismCrawl response body and status code, unchanged. Each call fetches one page. Use `page` to request later pages.
- **Source HTML** (PrismCrawl's `html` option) isn't exposed, because this Actor stores the normalized JSON. Use the [PrismCrawl API](https://www.prismcrawl.com/docs) directly if you need it.

## Errors and retries

The Actor reports PrismCrawl errors in the run's status message and log, including the PrismCrawl **request ID**:

| HTTP status | Meaning | Retried? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | Invalid request parameters | No |
| 401 | Missing, invalid, expired, or revoked API key | No |
| 402 | No PrismCrawl credits remaining | No |
| 429 | Rate limit exceeded | Yes, up to 3 times, waiting until the reported reset time (max 60 s) |
| 5xx | PrismCrawl could not complete the request | Yes, up to 3 times with exponential backoff |

Connection failures that never reached PrismCrawl (DNS errors, refused connections) are also retried. Retries only happen for failed requests, which PrismCrawl doesn't charge for, so a retry doesn't cause a duplicate charge. If a request times out, the Actor does **not** retry, because the request may have completed on PrismCrawl's side. Check your PrismCrawl request history before running again. If an error happens after some pages were saved, the run fails but the saved pages stay in the dataset.

## FAQ, disclaimers, and support

**Is this an independent scraper?** No. All requests are performed by the PrismCrawl API under your PrismCrawl account and subject to [PrismCrawl's terms](https://www.prismcrawl.com/terms). This Actor forwards your parameters and stores the response.

**Are results cached?** No. PrismCrawl runs a live request every time.

**Why did a lookup return no businesses?** If Yelp can't resolve the location, PrismCrawl returns a successful empty result with `location_not_found: true`. This still uses one credit, because the lookup completed.

**Where can I learn more?** The [PrismCrawl API documentation](https://www.prismcrawl.com/docs) covers every parameter and response field. PrismCrawl also offers search, maps, shopping, app store, and review endpoints at [prismcrawl.com](https://www.prismcrawl.com/).

**Support.** For problems with this Actor, open an issue in the **Issues** tab. For account, credit, or API questions, contact PrismCrawl at support@prismcrawl.com and include the request ID.

Make sure your use of this data complies with applicable laws and the terms of the services involved.
